explanation: The hypothesis identifies a relevant part of the target mechanism: fabrication-induced strain and edge-related pinning can influence nanostructure magnetism, and annealing can relieve strain. Its controlled annealed-versus-as-deposited comparison and explicit falsification rule are useful. However, it omits the specific 700 K Ar/N2 treatment, preservation of the amorphous or short-range-ordered structure, short-range atomic reordering, improved exchange alignment and ferromagnetic volume fraction, ribbon-spacing effects, and elastic-strain tests. It also substitutes unsupported predictions of a sharper transition, lower hysteresis, and faster cycling for the observed enhancement of magnetization and peak −ΔSM. The operating boundaries are vague and omit the pre-crystallization limit, 40–200 K conventional response, inverse response below 20 K, 0–2% elastic-strain limit, and spacing-dependent decoupling. The experiment could test the proposed hypothesis, but it would not cleanly distinguish strain relaxation from short-range chemical or magnetic reordering without more specific structural and magnetic measurements.
